No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Governor Yusuf Hints At Possible Divorce from Kwankwaso’s Daughter by Hafsat Bello Bahara 11 seconds ago in News Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram Kano State governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has sparked speculation that he may have agreed to end his marriage to his second wife, Zainab Musa Kwankwaso, following her decision to seek divorce through an Abuja court.
The governor made remarks interpreted as an indirect reference to the marital dispute during an event at the Kano Government House on Monday, where he appeared to suggest that he was ready to grant what he described as a “white paper” to bring the controversy to an end.
Although Yusuf did not mention his wife by name or explicitly announce a divorce, his choice of words and the white paper he held during the event attracted attention.
Speaking in Hausa, the governor said, “If all our opponents want is a white paper, let them have it so that everyone can have peace. We have also directed the Commissioner for Information to issue a statement so that we can have the vacancy filled by someone from a respectable family.”
The expression appeared to draw on a Hausa cultural reference in which a written declaration on white paper is associated with divorce.
His reference to filling a vacancy has further fuelled speculation that he was alluding to the possible dissolution of his marriage.
The remarks come days after Zainab, daughter of former Kano State Governor and Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, reportedly approached an Upper Area Court in Gudu, Abuja, seeking to dissolve their marriage through khul’i, an Islamic procedure initiated by a wife.
She is also reportedly willing to return the dowry paid by the governor when they married on July 29, 2006. The marriage produced six children.
The court has reportedly directed Yusuf to appear on November 17, 2026, in connection with the proceedings.
The governor’s latest comments have raised questions about whether he has agreed to the proposed separation. However, he has yet to make an explicit public confirmation that the marriage has been dissolved.
